product.name: Example product
product.audience: People completing one clearly named job

journey: Inspect evidence relevant to the decision
contentHierarchy: Concrete product promise and primary action
Fixture-backed proof in the signature element

candidates.thesis: A quiet editorial frame organized around one real working artifact.
candidates.composition: Asymmetric narrative column paired with a dense product workbench.
candidates.typography: Expressive serif-like display rhythm with a compact sans-serif body.
candidates.palette: Paper neutrals, dark ink, and one annotation accent.
candidates.signatureElement: An inspectable product artifact carrying real fixture content.

candidates.thesis: A precise reference index that makes comparison the visual story.
candidates.composition: Dense ruled rows and marginal labels with almost no card containers.
candidates.typography: Narrow display labels paired with highly legible tabular body text.
candidates.palette: Cool monochrome surfaces with status colors used only as data.
candidates.signatureElement: A live comparison index with a persistent reading cursor.

candidates.thesis: A warm, human proof wall built from outcomes and annotated evidence.
candidates.composition: Overlapping editorial fragments anchored by one clear action column.
candidates.typography: Friendly grotesk headlines with restrained handwritten annotations.
candidates.palette: Warm off-white, charcoal, and a tactile print-inspired accent.
candidates.signatureElement: A layered proof wall made from licensed or product-owned assets.

selectedDirection.rationale: It makes the product itself the proof while preserving a direct reading order and modest asset budget.

rejections.reason: Its comparison density overstates the amount of structured product data on this route.
Its asset dependence would compete with the working artifact and slow responsive delivery.

refinementVariants.change: Give the workbench the first viewport's dominant area and compress supporting copy.
refinementVariants.tradeoff: Stronger proof, but less room to explain an unfamiliar category.

refinementVariants.change: Lead with a compact product narrative before revealing the full workbench.
refinementVariants.tradeoff: Clearer category framing, but the product proof arrives later.

selectedVariant.rationale: The audience already understands the category and needs evidence of a specific product advantage.

visualThesis: Editorial restraint with one product-specific working surface, not a generic SaaS montage.
signatureElement: A real, fixture-backed product artifact that carries the page's primary proof.

states.description: Public landing state with deterministic content

interactions.name: Start
interactions.purpose: Advance to the product's first meaningful task

references.title: A directly inspected reference
references.lesson: Name the transferable hierarchy or interaction lesson; do not copy its composition or assets.

tokens.typography: One expressive display face paired with a highly legible body face.
tokens.palette: A calm neutral base with one semantic accent tied to product meaning.
tokens.density: Compact around controls and evidence; more open around the primary narrative transition.
tokens.shapeLanguage: Mostly square working surfaces with restrained rounding on interactive controls.

motionBudget.purpose: Motion explains a state change or directs attention to the signature element.

componentSources.decision: Reuse and wrap; do not edit the vendor primitive.

responsiveIntent.narrow: Recompose into one reading column; keep the primary action and proof visible without horizontal scrolling.
responsiveIntent.tablet: Preserve hierarchy while introducing the first useful side-by-side relationship.
responsiveIntent.desktop: Use width for stronger composition and evidence density, not simply larger empty margins.

accessibilityConstraints: One main landmark and a coherent heading order
Every meaningful interaction is named and keyboard reachable
No horizontal overflow at 320 CSS pixels
antiGoals: No repeated card grid without content-driven grouping
No motion that competes with the signature element
